notes:
Account summary: Citrus Arc ML is a mid-market SaaS company building in-product semantic search and insight surfaces for B2B product analytics. Primary goal: replace noisy keyword search with semantic retrieval for help center, in-app search, and workspace-wide document discovery. They run large nightly batch jobs to embed event logs and docs (nightly delta ~120k docs) and require real-time semantic search for end-user queries (peak traffic window during business hours).

POC scope (hosted -> dedicated): They kicked off a Hosted API POC to validate embeddings quality and end-to-end latency with their vector DB. If perf and cost align, they want to move to Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and lower per-embedding cost.

Technical targets and constraints:
- Corpus: initial 1.2M documents, average document length ~250 tokens. Nightly delta ~120k docs.
- Batch embedding SLA: complete nightly run within a 2–3 hour maintenance window => need ~60k embeddings/hour sustained (target 70k/hr to include retries).
- Real-time search SLA: p95 search latency target <= 150ms for user-facing queries; expected peak qps ~600, sustained 200–300 qps outside peaks.
- Embedding model: prefer an open/Redwood-verified embedding with 768-dim vectors for storage cost reasons; willing to test higher-dim if quality delta is material.
- Vector DB integration: currently POC with Pinecone; evaluating a Redwood native connector to reduce transfer steps and to test prefix/KV caching impact on search latency.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance, customer-managed KMS (rotations), and audit log retention for 13 months; data residency needs US/EU options.

POC observations so far:
- 2026-01-27: initial hosted-API bulk ingest: ~15k embeddings/hr (single-threaded). Bottleneck identified as small batch sizes and single-worker concurrency.
- 2026-02-05: after SE tuning (Liam): adjusted batch size to 512, parallelized 6 workers -> observed sustained 68k embeddings/hr via bulk endpoint. Good headroom but cost increased due to concurrency.
- Search perf: baseline p95 ~180ms with default routing and cache settings; after KV-cache tuning and routing to nearest region p95 down to ~130ms. Still want <120ms for 95th.
- Nightly job stability: occasional 5–7 minute spikes when large docs trigger longer tokenization paths. Considering truncation/segmenting policy.

Commercial/Procurement notes:
- They are price-sensitive; projecting ARR target between $50k–$200k. Interested in 12-month reserved committed capacity if unit economics are clearer.
- Main negotiation points: per-embedding unit price at scale, included throughput tiers for Dedicated, and burst vs baseline commit.

Security & legal:
- Security team requested detailed KMS handling doc, SOC2 scope, and proof of audit log retention. Also asked about contractual language for key custody and emergency key rotation procedures.

Next steps (owner & dates):
- SE (Liam): finalize Dedicated perf baseline report (run on Dedicated staging nodes) by 2026-02-28.
- AE (Maya): deliver updated pricing worksheet with 12-month commit and blended usage model by 2026-02-22.
- Security: schedule follow-up to validate KMS policy with Citrus Arc security (target meeting 2026-02-24).

Quote from customer (call 2026-02-15): "We need the nightly job to finish before our morning analytics window — otherwise teams are blocked. Also, show us a Dedicated plan that materially reduces our cost compared to the hosted run."

Open risks/blockers: throughput for nightly batch still borderline if concurrency increases cost; procurement needs an example SOW for Dedicated onboarding; security sign-off on KMS rotation is a gating item.
